@dataclass
class User:
    """Represents an application user account.

    A ``User`` bundles identity, contact, and ownership state for a single
    account in the benchmark application. Instances are dataclasses, so
    equality and ``repr`` are derived from the field values.

    Attributes:
        id: Stable integer identifier for the user.
        email: Email address used for login and contact.
        name: Human-readable display name.
        active: Whether the account is currently enabled. Defaults to ``True``.
        item_ids: Identifiers of items owned by this user. Defaults to an
            empty list.

    Methods:
        can_login: Return ``True`` when the account is active and the email
            looks structurally valid (contains ``"@"``).
        owns_item: Return ``True`` when the given ``item_id`` is in this
            user's ``item_ids``.

    Example:
        >>> user = User(id=1, email="ada@example.com", name="Ada", item_ids=[10])
        >>> user.can_login()
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(10)
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(99)
        False
    """

    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    active: bool = True
    item_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    def can_login(self) -> bool:
        return self.active and "@" in self.email

    def owns_item(self, item_id: int) -> bool:
        return item_id in self.item_ids
